notes: Czech read by a Polish speaker. The skeletons collapse the regular West Slavic orthographic correspondences: Czech h answers Polish g (hlava/glowa), Czech caron digraphs answer Polish di/trigraphs (c/cz, s/sz, z/z), Polish l answers Czech l, and the Polish nasals answer Czech oral vowels. Measured effect on the 3000-word Czech speech deck: hlavni/glowny rises from 0.17 to 0.83, horsi/gorszy from 0.50 to 1.00. Digraph rules must precede their component letters. The floor/weight split is per-pair calibration against the app's three sensitivity stops (0.95 loose, 0.85 default, 0.75 strict), which were originally set for Spanish's raw-similarity scale. At 0.55/0.45 the combined score compressed so far that the loose stop hid two words; 0.75/0.25 puts kazdy/kazdy, skola/szkola and znovu/znowu at the default stop, which is the same 'obvious cognates' meaning Spanish has there. Ordering is unchanged by this: it stretches the scale, it does not reweight the evidence. default_threshold is the auto cutoff for this pair, chosen by reading the scored word list band by band on the 3000-word Czech deck: quality holds down to 0.70 (ctyri/cztery, koupit/kupic, trik/trick) and turns mixed at 0.65 (osobni/osobowy, stal/stay). Nothing is lost below it — excluded words move to Extras, so the cost of the number being slightly wrong is that a learner sees a word they already knew.
